rtl_snippet: always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrst_n) begin

fix.rationale:
Tracing the path: startpoint _124902_ is DFF_X1 attributed to uart_rx.v:170, which lands inside the p_cycle_counter always block (the block header is the nearest attributable line), i.e. this is a cycle_counter bit. From there the only combinational fan-out in this module is: cycle_counter -> next_bit (equality compares, matches the NOR4/NAND4-ish first cells) -> the case-based n_fsm_state mux (p_n_fsm_state, FSM_STOP arm) -> the original uart_rx_valid expression "fsm_state==FSM_STOP && n_fsm_state==FSM_IDLE" -> out of this module into uart_wrapper's fifo2_winc (~fifo2_wfull && uart_rx_valid) -> async_fifo/wptr_full.v's binary-increment + gray-encode + wfull comparator (matches the OAI22/AOI211/AND3/AND3/NAND3/XOR2x3/NOR3 tail) -> the wfull DFFR endpoint at wptr_full.v:52.

RETIME is not available: there is no register sitting inside this combinational chain between cycle_counter and the wfull register that could be relocated - fsm_state is already a register present at the start of the case evaluation, and next_bit/n_fsm_state/uart_rx_valid are all pure combinational with no intervening flop to shift.

PIPELINE was rejected because most of the depth (the adder/gray-code/comparator tail) and the fanout consumer (fifo2_winc, wfull, and the mirrored full/empty logic used by the read side of the FIFO) live in uart_wrapper.v and wptr_full.v, both out of my edit scope. Inserting a new register in uart_rx.v to delay uart_rx_valid by a cycle would shift when uart_rx_data/uart_rx_break/uart_rx_valid become visible to the wrapper and would require re-balancing fifo2_winc, rptr synchronization, and the RX-side consumer logic in files I'm not permitted to touch - correctness there can't be verified from this scope.

RESTRUCTURE is available and provably exact: the case statement's FSM_STOP arm defines n_fsm_state = next_bit ? FSM_IDLE : FSM_STOP. Since FSM_IDLE (0) and FSM_STOP (3) are distinct encodings, "n_fsm_state==FSM_IDLE" is true exactly when next_bit==1, for every value of fsm_state where the outer AND term (fsm_state==FSM_STOP) is also true; when fsm_state!=FSM_STOP both the old and new expressions are forced to 0 by that same AND term. So `uart_rx_valid = (fsm_state==FSM_STOP) && next_bit` is bit-exact equivalent to the original `(fsm_state==FSM_STOP) && (n_fsm_state==FSM_IDLE)` for all reachable and unreachable state encodings alike - it isn't a "typical inputs" approximation. This removes the n_fsm_state 3-bit mux/decode plus the subsequent 3-bit equality-to-zero compare from the fan-in of uart_rx_valid, replacing it with the single-bit `next_bit` signal that already exists (computed once, reused by the case statement itself, so no new logic is introduced elsewhere). This shortens exactly the front portion of the reported critical chain while leaving cycle count, uart_rx_data, uart_rx_break, and all downstream consumers (uart_rx_valid's value into fifo2_winc, etc.) functionally identical every cycle, so no reconvergent-path rebalancing is needed. Latency is unchanged, hence added_latency_cycles = 0.
